messages:
anya: bringing up butterfly13b (int4, per-channel quant) on canary. seeing OOMs at ~180 concurrent requests on 2xA100-40G. also tail latency spikes. logs show cuda OOM in KV cache alloc.

jordan: root cause looks like KV cache + batching growth. what's current max_new_tokens and batch limits?

anya: default max_new_tokens set to 512 in model config; batch_size=8; adaptive window=auto; prefetch enabled. can reproduce with stress harness: 50 threads, prompt len 200.

leo: try lowering max_new_tokens to 128 and reduce batch_size to 4. also disable prefetch for int4; int4 KV growth worse. can we test using smaller kv_reserve?

leo: ```
model_config:
  max_new_tokens: 128
  batch_size: 4
  prefetch: false
  kv_reserve: 0.12
```

nisha: note: quality regressions seen when int4 + aggressive kv_trim. run eval harness vs fp16 on common prompts before changing defaults. :eyes: 

anya: ran quick eval: int4 BLEU-like metric dropped 1.8% vs fp16 on summarization set when max_new_tokens capped at 128; but latency improves 30%. attaching numbers in thread.

jordan: we can try asymmetric quant profile (outliers preserved) + enable per-layer scales — reduces quality loss. Also try windowed batching: max_new_tokens per-request cap + per-model burst token cap.

leo: also memory fragmentation likely — use defrag on coldstart and smaller microbatching. command to force defrag on runtime: `./runtimectl defrag --model butterfly13b`

deploy-bot: canary deploy 4923456795: butterfly13b-int4-v1 rolled to 10% capacity — health OK

anya: Plan: 1) run 2x tests: (a) max_new 128, batch 4, prefetch off, per-layer scale; (b) keep 512 but kv_reserve 0.08 and add defrag on instance start. 2) run eval harness and perf bench. 3) if quality delta >1% revert quant profile. assigning: leo->perf, jordan->quant, nisha->evals. I'll coordinate rollout. :thumbsup:

jordan: I'll push quant profile PR and upload eval plots to drive. ping me when canary at 10% to watch OOM metrics.

leo: starting perf run now, will post logs. early sign: microbatching reduced tail latency but increased throughput a bit.
